title: incident-bot: surface SLO hinting & slo-toolkit hint utilities for on-call runbook suggestions
author: Sarah Chen
description:
Motivation: On-call responders frequently need quick, high-signal SLO context when investigating incidents. This PR adds SLO hint extraction in incident-bot and exposes a small, well-tested hint utilities module in slo-toolkit so runbook suggestions and diagnostics can surface compact, prioritized SLO hints (e.g., error budget remaining, burn rate, recent windowed breaches).

What this changes: Adds runtime extraction of compact SLO hints to the incident-bot event pipeline, new SLO hint utilities in slo-toolkit (ranking, compact formatter, TTL caching helpers), instrumentation for telemetry (histograms for hint generation latency), and docs + runbook metadata updates so runbook suggestion logic can opt into showing these hints. Includes unit and integration tests and feature flags for gradual rollout.

Checklist: - [x] core extraction logic implemented in incident-bot - [x] hinting utilities and unit tests added to slo-toolkit - [x] lightweight integration test in perf-canary to validate end-to-end hint surface - [x] docs updated (runbooks + incident-bot operational playbook) - [x] feature gated behind ff:incident_slo_hints

Testing notes: Local unit test suite added (slo-toolkit/tests/test_hints.py). Integration smoke runs against staging SLO API included; a flaky KPI in one e2e run caused a rerun in CI which passed. Manual verification steps are documented in the PR description and runbook fragment.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged on by default in staging for two weeks, then enable for 10% of production incidents for two days, monitor hint generation latency and any increase in incident-bot errors (alerting hooks added). If safe, increase to 100% and include hints in on-call Slack messages.

Related: ENG-4012 (SLO UX improvements), SUP-7891 (customer escalations requesting quicker SLO context).
